Tweedie outcomes checked with a Gaussian model

A model can reproduce correlation but miss other features

These simulated Tweedie outcomes are nonnegative and skewed, with some zeros and different variability for women and men. We deliberately fit an exchangeable Gaussian model: the same effects and variance for both roles. Its shared dyad intercept allows positive partner correlation; there is no member-difference random effect, but observation-level variance is still estimated.

Every code chunk below runs when this document is rendered. Each check is followed by all the complete panels it produces, in their original order.

Fit the model and simulate once

Run from dev/diagnostic_checks/ to read the saved dataset of 120 female-male dyads. All checks reuse the same 2,000 simulated datasets.

library(dyadMLM)
tweedie_data <- read.csv(
  "distribution-diagnostics/results/tweedie-gaussian/data.csv",
  colClasses = c(role = "factor")
)
tweedie_data$dyad <- factor(tweedie_data$dyad)
gaussian_model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  outcome ~ predictor + (1 | dyad),
  family = gaussian(), dispformula = ~1, data = tweedie_data
)
gaussian_simulations <- simulate_dyad_responses(
  gaussian_model, nsim = 2000, seed = 100105
)

Supply the fitting data because role is absent from the model frame. Roles split the plots without changing the fitted model’s assumptions.

Check residuals

predictors adds a page for the named predictor; details = TRUE adds the uniformity and PIT-distance page. The call produces three complete panels.

check_residuals(
  gaussian_simulations, dyad = dyad, role = role, data = tweedie_data,
  predictors = "predictor",
  details = TRUE, seed = 123, ask = FALSE
)

The QQ curves and PIT histogram reveal a distribution mismatch. Five male outcomes fall outside all their reference simulations, compared with a usual simulated count of zero to one. Predicted outcome means the model prediction with random effects set to zero. The separate predictor page uses the supplied predictor values. Red quartiles should roughly follow the horizontal lines at 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75, usually within their matching blue bands.

Check outcomes

check_zeros = TRUE includes zero counts; centred_overlay = TRUE adds the distribution after subtracting predictions. The call produces two complete panels.

check_outcomes(
  gaussian_simulations, dyad = dyad, role = role, data = tweedie_data,
  check_zeros = TRUE, centred_overlay = TRUE, ask = FALSE
)

The Gaussian model generates negative values, misses the male zeros, and understates the largest deviations from predictions. Its common variance is too large for female responses and too small for male responses.

Check partner dependence

The default check subtracts the same predictions from observed and simulated outcomes. It produces one complete panel for this composition.

check_partner_dependence(
  gaussian_simulations, dyad = dyad, role = role,
  data = tweedie_data, ask = FALSE
)

The role SDs and mean–difference correlation reveal unequal variability, while the partner correlation agrees reasonably well. Omitting the difference random effect does not by itself force a mismatch: the shared intercept and observation-level noise can reproduce positive partner correlation.

For comparison, request the same panel for raw outcomes:

check_partner_dependence(
  gaussian_simulations, dyad = dyad, role = role, data = tweedie_data,
  response = "raw", ask = FALSE
)

This includes variation explained by the predictor; the role-variance mismatch remains visible. Several assumptions are wrong here, so a failed check does not identify a single cause. Blue ranges describe the middle 95% at each comparison, not across all plots. These are descriptive checks, not significance tests.
